overallReasoning.summary: Use one real Foundry model behind APIM, compare project Responses with known-working Chat Completions, measure actual backend usage and APIM enforcement, then evaluate mitigations separately.
overallReasoning.tradeoffs: The existing resource group's West US metadata does not constrain its resources. East US 2 has verified model deployment and quota. Both classic and v2 gateways are now deployed for comparison. Public networking and recurring costs were explicitly approved. No App Insights, Log Analytics, Key Vault, VNet, or private endpoints were required. Customer model/version, region, effective policy, and gateway topology remain unknown; production hardening is not claimed.

plan.validation: Corrected full Incremental deployment verified Succeeded; Bicep compilation succeeded; 21 focused unit tests passed. Complete exact project-v1 Responses versus project-v1 Chat suites passed on classic and v2 gateways. Quota/TPM and request-throttle rejections were trace-confirmed as gateway-origin. Native rate protection was confirmed with backend-origin 429s. Final live inspection verified both identity gates, all 12 operation token policies, disabled local authentication, managed identity configuration, restored model capacity 100, and invalid-subscription 401 on both gateways. No automated security scanner was installed or run.
architecturePrinciples: No modifications outside the authorized resource group.
No patient data or credentials in persisted evidence.
Preserve the baseline before policy changes.
Distinguish mitigation, reporting behavior, actual enforcement, and proven causal resolution.
Do not remove existing controls until replacement protection is measured.

costEstimate.modelUsage: Pay per token, additional to gateway pricing. Use bounded synthetic requests, modest output limits, and an explicit test-call ceiling.
costEstimate.exclusions: Taxes, egress, optional networking, monitoring, and account-specific discounts. These are retail estimates, not measured billing.
costEstimate.currentLabSpendFromThisTask: Both gateways, a Foundry account/project, and a real model deployment now exist and incur charges. Both gateways together are about USD 6.51/day retail plus model tokens and applicable extras. Actual billing has not been queried. No automated expiry is configured.

experiment.additionalBoundedBatch: The original preview study was bounded to 120 persisted calls. The exact project v1 Responses route became available later, so a second bounded validation batch was explicitly allocated under the user's existing resource/cost approval using --max-total-calls 240. The harness default remains 120. No call or model-token traffic is unbounded.
baseline: Record gateway tier, region, effective policies, stable APIM subscription/caller identity, unique test counter keys, model version, and route.

Preserve the initial project v1 Responses 404 as historical evidence. That endpoint later returned 200; no specific causal fix for the transient 404 was isolated. After verifying restored backend headers, compare exact project v1 Responses with exact project v1 Chat on both gateway generations. Preview comparisons remain separately labeled.
Compare with Chat Completions on the same model and equivalent policy settings; use account-level Chat if project Chat is unsupported and record this difference.
Capture UTC timestamps, request IDs, APIM trace IDs, actual backend usage before transformations, policy accounting headers, status, and policy errors.
Run sequential calls in isolated counters and track time to avoid confusing TPM replenishment or quota rollover with accounting failure.
enforcement: Test quota and TPM separately with low limits on fresh test counters.
Require policy-generated 403 for quota exhaustion and 429 for TPM exhaustion, confirmed in traces rather than inferred from status alone.
Allow a completed request to update actual usage before evaluating subsequent calls.
Compare estimate-prompt-tokens=true and false only after preserving the original baseline.
If necessary, compare account-level Responses and a v2 gateway to narrow whether project routing or gateway generation matters.
mitigations: Apply request-based throttling to Responses only with a stable caller key; verify APIM-generated throttling and unchanged Chat Completions behavior.
Treat request throttling as a request-rate safeguard, not a token quota or spend guarantee.
Determine whether the proposed Foundry project/model fallback uses the same APIM gateway and llm-token-limit implementation.
Validate any allegedly independent fallback on the exact project route before removing the original token policy.
Preserve authentication and inherited protections; do not remove base policy inheritance as a shortcut.
Restore a documented safe policy state after experiments.

decisionRules.reproduced: Actual backend usage exceeds the estimate, policy counters remain flat, and crossed limits are not enforced on subsequent completed calls while the matched control works.
decisionRules.reportingOnly: Backend usage is correctly enforced but response accounting headers are stale or overwritten.
decisionRules.notReproduced: Both routes show expected actual usage accounting and validated quota/TPM enforcement; document lab/customer differences and do not claim the customer's case is resolved.
decisionRules.confirmedFix: A specifically identified change restores measured accounting and enforcement on the previously failing route, with before/after evidence.
decisionRules.mitigationOnly: Request throttling works but actual token enforcement remains broken or unverified.

experiment.conclusions: The flat-4 defect was not reproduced. Complete exact-v1 suites on both gateway generations report 167 actual and consumed tokens, reject 220-token quota traffic with APIM 403, and reject 300-TPM traffic with APIM 429 on both project Responses and project Chat. Operation-only 3/60s request throttling rejects the fourth classic call and fifth v2 call without affecting Chat; it is approximate mitigation, not a token-accounting fix. Some remaining-quota headers were stale/non-monotonic despite working enforcement. Backend-origin 429s established independent native rate protection, not per-project hourly quotas. Initial v1 404 cleared without an isolated causal fix. Quota changes propagated asynchronously and were verified in data-plane headers before exact-route tests. All temporary controls were restored and live-verified. Keep/reopen the customer case until its exact failing environment is validated; no customer root cause or causal fix is claimed.
